Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary To calculate the score of your hand, or the final score, first sort the cards by Yokai type, and then add up the lowest card of each Yokai type. The player with the lowest final score wins the game. In case of a tie, the player with the fewest different types of Yokai wins. If there is still a tie, the player with the fewest total cards wins. community_text:
[Rating: 3/10] Yokai Pagoda is in large part a memory and card-counting game. I do not do well at or enjoy those, so my score is entirely my subjective experience and not a comment on the game's quality: It does what it does very well and the art is beautiful. However personally, I simply cannot vibe with memory games! If you DO, I highly recommend trying this.

[Rating: 3/10] clever idea to try to minize your points over multiple rounds - strategizing around that feels really good. Or it would, if it wasn't was for the insane amount of luck / randomness.

[Rating: 3/10] It falls flat when everyone doesn't know each other score during the 3 rounds of play.

[Rating: 4/10] Play matching cards to piles to dump cards on others, try to collect as few cards as possible while limiting the suits you're stuck with. Doesn't work well online since you aren't seeing what others are getting. Not something I care enough to try in person.

[Rating: 5/10] Either this is a copy of Mojo, or Mojo is a copy of this game. Either way, both are average games. I would have liked at least one of the two games not to try to copy, but to develop the idea further.
